title: How is the US economy really doing under President Trump?
summary:
President Donald Trump has been boasting about the performance of the US economy ahead of the midterm congressional elections, claiming he has boosted incomes, reduced inflation and created jobs.
Trump has repeatedly said: "We have the hottest country anywhere in the world."
The US economy is also being helped by an AI investment boom, and could falter if that spending were to dry up.
So how does all this feel for the average American?
BBC Verify has looked at whether the evidence supports the president's claims.

title: Gas and Oil Prices Soar As Trump Deals With Iran War, Inflation
summary:
It's expensive out there: Gas prices have been stuck at over $4 a gallon for more days this year than any other.
Since the Iran war first kicked off in February and the Strait was subsequently closed, gas and oil prices have skyrocketed.
Trump has highlighted the broader goals of the war and argued that the increase in gas prices would be transient.
After the start of the war in February, crude oil prices soared and remain significantly higher than when Trump's second term began.
Long gone are the days of gas stations touting below-$3 prices; prices are still hovering in the mid-$4 range.

title: Homebuyers are canceling sales at near-record rates
summary:
Homebuyers are backing out of contracts at near-record rates, a potential sign of how higher mortgage rates are prompting buyers to rethink their plans.
But pending sales tend to fall through at higher rates when buyers have more options and more negotiating power, as they currently do in much of the country.
Indeed, metro areas that are notably buyer's markets, like Jacksonville and Tampa, Fla., and Las Vegas, all had contract cancellation rates approaching 20%, higher than anywhere else in the country.
But they're relatively rare in strong seller's markets like San Francisco, where just 2.8% of deals fell apart.
Claire Boston is a Senior Reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

title: Housing Market Warning: Homebuilder Sentiment Drops to 14-Year Low
summary:
Homebuilder sentiment fell three points to 29 in October, according to the National Association of Home Builders/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index.
October's reading marks the lowest homebuilder sentiment the US has seen since June 2012, the NAHB said, when the housing market was still moving through the aftermath of the 2008 crisis.
Here's what explains the decline:The housing market is frozen.
Add to Preferred SourcesThe Housing Market Index remains well-below the midway threshold of 50, which suggests that homebuilding is solidly in contractional territory.
Sara Godfrey, an economist at Oxford Economics, said the latest "depressed" homebuilder sentiment reading was consistent with the firm's view that the housing market would remain stagnant all throughout next year.
